text: I'm going to go with my hottest take, and this is the take that I have the least evidence for. So let's just start with that.
speaker: Dan Shipper
context: Lenny asks Dan what he believes about AI that most people don't believe. Dan shares his most contrarian prediction about AI's impact on employment. While many people worry about AI eliminating jobs, Dan believes AI could actually bring jobs back to America by making expensive services affordable for smaller companies and allowing American workers to serve more customers efficiently using AI tools.
text_ko: 가장 파격적인 의견부터 말씀드릴게요. 솔직히 이건 제가 근거가 제일 약한 주장이에요. 그럼 바로 그 얘기부터 시작할게요.
text_zh: 我要说一个最大胆的观点，而且这个观点我手头的证据是最少的。咱们就从这个开始吧。
text_es: Voy a ir con mi opinión más polémica, y es la que menos evidencia tengo para respaldar. Así que empecemos por ahí.
key_sentence: I'm going to go with my hottest take, and this is the take that I have the least evidence for.
original_text: I'm going to go with my hottest take, and this is the take that I have the least evidence for. So let's just start with that. I have other more well-reasoned takes to give you, but this is my hottest one, which is I think that AI may be one of the biggest force for reshoring American jobs.

vocabulary.definition: A bold or provocative opinion or assertion, often made without substantial evidence or support.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, particularly in brainstorming or strategy sessions, a 'hottest take' can stimulate debate and encourage innovative thinking, even if the idea lacks empirical backing.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can spark creativity, using a 'hottest take' may also risk undermining credibility if not supported by data.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the minimal amount of proof or support available for a claim or opinion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In decision-making processes, stating that a claim has the 'least evidence' highlights the need for further research or validation before acting on that claim.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase can imply skepticism and caution, suggesting that the idea may not be reliable or actionable.

text: And what I noticed with him is he was just making a year. He made a year's worth of progress in two months because every time I sat down with him and told him, okay, here's how you tell a story.
speaker: Dan Shipper
context: Dan is explaining why he disagrees with headlines saying AI will eliminate entry-level jobs. He describes working with a young employee named Alex who accelerated his learning dramatically by using AI. Instead of traditional mentoring where people repeat mistakes, this employee recorded all feedback, converted it into prompts, and used AI to avoid making the same errors repeatedly.
text_ko: 제가 그 사람에게서 본 건, 그는 그냥 1년치 진전을 두 달 만에 이뤘다는 거예요. 제가 그와 앉아서 "이렇게 스토리텔링(storytelling)하면 돼요"라고 말할 때마다요.
text_zh: 我发现他的情况是这样的，他简直就是在飞速进步。两个月的时间就相当于别人一年的进步，因为每次我跟他坐下来聊，告诉他"你看，讲故事应该这样讲"的时候。
text_es: Y lo que me di cuenta con él es que avanzó lo que normalmente tomaría un año entero. Hizo el progreso de todo un año en solo dos meses porque cada vez que me sentaba con él y le decía, "mira, así es como tienes que contar una historia."
key_sentence: He made a year's worth of progress in two months, never making the same mistake twice.
original_text: And what I noticed with him is he was just making a year. He made a year's worth of progress in two months because every time I sat down with him and told him, okay, here's how you tell a story. Here's how you think about a headline. He recorded all of it, put it into a prompt, and he never made the same mistake twice.

vocabulary.definition: The advancement or improvement in a particular area or task over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, progress is often measured in terms of project milestones, sales growth, or skill development among employees.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'progress' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply that there is still work to be done, so it is important to use it in contexts where improvement is expected.

text: We have a head of AI operations. I sit with her once a week. And every time I'm doing something repetitively, we put it in a to-do list.
speaker: Dan Shipper
context: Lenny asks Dan about how his 15-person team operates so efficiently across multiple products and a consulting business. Dan explains their key innovation of having a dedicated AI operations person whose job is to identify repetitive tasks across the organization and build AI automations for them, allowing everyone to focus on higher-value work instead of manual processes.
text_ko: 저는 AI 운영 총괄(Head of AI Operations)과 매주 한 번 앉아서 얘기해요. 그리고 반복적으로 하는 일이 생기면 그때그때 할 일 목록(to-do list)에 적어둬요.
text_zh: 我们有个AI运营负责人。我每周都会跟她坐下来聊一次。每次我发现自己在重复做某件事的时候，我们就把它加到待办清单里。
text_es: Tenemos una jefa de operaciones de IA. Me reúno con ella una vez a la semana. Y cada vez que estoy haciendo algo repetitivo, lo apuntamos en una lista de pendientes.
key_sentence: And every time I'm doing something repetitively, we put it in a to-do list.
original_text: We have a head of AI operations. I sit with her once a week. And every time I'm doing something repetitively, we put it in a to-do list. And she's just constantly building prompts and building workflows that I and everyone else on the team are just automating as much as possible.

vocabulary.definition: The activities involved in the day-to-day functioning of a business, including production, logistics, and management processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, 'operations' refers to the systematic processes that ensure efficiency and effectiveness in delivering products or services.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'operations' can imply routine tasks, it also encompasses strategic planning and resource management, making it a critical aspect of organizational success.

text: One of the things that we do that I think is really cool, and they basically invented this, I had nothing to do with this, is they invented the idea of compounding engineering.
speaker: Dan Shipper
context: Dan is describing innovative engineering practices his team uses. His engineers Kieran and Nityesh developed this concept where instead of just completing tasks, they build tools and prompts that make similar future tasks easier. This creates a compound effect where the team becomes more efficient over time rather than just maintaining the same productivity level.
text_ko: 제가 보기에는 우리가 하는 일 중 정말 멋진 것 하나가 있는데, 사실 이건 거의 그들이 발명한 거예요. 저는 전혀 관여하지 않았고, 그들이 '컴파운딩 엔지니어링(compounding engineering)'이라는 개념을 만들어 냈어요.
text_zh: 我们做的一件特别酷的事情，这个完全是他们想出来的，我没参与，就是他们发明了复合工程(compounding engineering)这个概念。
text_es: Una de las cosas que hacemos que me parece genial, y básicamente ellos inventaron esto, yo no tuve nada que ver, es que inventaron el concepto de ingeniería compuesta (compounding engineering).
key_sentence: they invented the idea of compounding engineering.
original_text: One of the things that we do that I think is really cool, and they basically invented this, I had nothing to do with this, is they invented the idea of compounding engineering. So basically, for every unit of work, you should make the next unit of work easier to do.

vocabulary.definition: The application of scientific and mathematical principles to design, build, and analyze structures, machines, and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology firms, engineering is fundamental for product development and operational efficiency, often driving innovation and scalability.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a level of technical expertise and problem-solving ability, and is often associated with precision and systematic approaches.

vocabulary.definition: The process of combining multiple elements or factors to create a cumulative effect, often leading to exponential growth or improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, compounding can refer to the accumulation of knowledge, resources, or customer loyalty that enhances overall performance and market position over time.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts, and is frequently used in financial contexts as well.

text: I think the number one predictor is, does the CEO use ChatGPT, or insert your own chatbot. If the CEO is in it all the time, being like, this is the coolest thing, everybody else is going to start doing it.
speaker: Dan Shipper
context: Lenny asks what separates companies that successfully adopt AI from those that don't, based on Dan's consulting experience with large organizations. Dan shares his most reliable predictor for AI adoption success. He explains that CEO engagement with AI tools directly determines whether the entire organization will embrace these technologies, because leaders need both excitement and realistic expectations that only come from hands-on experience.
text_ko: 제일 큰 예측 변수는 CEO가 챗GPT(ChatGPT)나 다른 챗봇(chatbot)을 직접 쓰느냐예요. CEO가 늘 '이거 진짜 최고야' 하면서 계속 사용하면, 다른 사람들도 금방 따라 하기 시작해요.
text_zh: 我觉得最能预测的指标就是，CEO本人用不用ChatGPT，或者换成别的聊天机器人(chatbot)也行。如果CEO自己天天在那儿用，觉得这玩意儿太酷了，那其他人肯定也会跟着用起来。
text_es: Creo que el factor que más predice el éxito es si el CEO usa ChatGPT, o el chatbot que sea. Si el CEO está todo el tiempo metiéndose ahí, diciendo "esto es lo más genial que hay", entonces todo el equipo va a empezar a usarlo también.
key_sentence: The number one predictor is CEO engagement with ChatGPT to lead that charge.
original_text: I think the number one predictor is, does the CEO use ChatGPT, or insert your own chatbot. If the CEO is in it all the time, being like, this is the coolest thing, everybody else is going to start doing it. If the CEO is like, I don't know, this is for someone else, no one else is going to be able to lead that charge.

vocabulary.definition: A predictor is a factor or variable that can be used to forecast or anticipate a future event or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, predictors are often used in data analysis and market research to identify trends and make informed decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'predictor' is often associated with statistical models, it can also imply a degree of uncertainty regarding future events.

text: And what I noticed using, at the time, like GPT-3 or maybe GPT-4, was that I was spending a lot of time, for example, thinking about, how do I communicate the problem? How do I gather the right information for the problem?
speaker: Dan Shipper
context: Dan explains his "allocation economy" thesis - his prediction that we're moving from a knowledge economy to one where management skills become more valuable. He describes how using AI tools early on made him realize he was spending time on tasks that mirror traditional management: communicating problems clearly, gathering information, providing feedback, and coordinating between different capabilities.
text_ko: 그때 제가 사용하던 모델(예: GPT-3, GPT-4)을 써보면서 느낀 건, 예를 들어 문제를 어떻게 전달할지, 문제 해결에 필요한 정확한 정보를 어떻게 모을지 같은 데 많은 시간을 쓰고 있다는 거였어요.
text_zh: 我当时用GPT-3或者GPT-4的时候发现，我花了很多时间在想，怎么把问题说清楚？怎么收集到解决问题需要的信息？
text_es: Y lo que me di cuenta usando, en ese momento, como GPT-3 o tal vez GPT-4, era que estaba perdiendo mucho tiempo, por ejemplo, pensando en, ¿cómo le explico el problema? ¿Cómo reúno la información correcta para el problema?
key_sentence: how do I communicate the problem? How do I gather the right information for the problem?
original_text: And what I noticed using, at the time, like GPT-3 or maybe GPT-4, was that I was spending a lot of time, for example, thinking about, how do I communicate the problem? How do I gather the right information for the problem? How do I put it in the right way so that the model that I'm working with gets it?

vocabulary.definition: To convey information or express thoughts and feelings through verbal, written, or non-verbal means.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, effective communication is crucial for collaboration, problem-solving, and ensuring that all team members are aligned with organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'communicate' is a general term, it is often used in contexts that emphasize clarity and effectiveness, distinguishing it from mere information sharing.

vocabulary.definition: To collect or assemble information, data, or resources from various sources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business or tech environment, gathering information is essential for decision-making, market research, and identifying customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'gather' implies a proactive effort to compile relevant information, as opposed to passively receiving it.
